pharm: A topical heparinoid (mucopolysaccharide polysulfuric acid ester) with heparin-like anticoagulant, fibrinolytic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-exudative properties, used on the skin for superficial venous and soft-tissue conditions. Minimal systemic absorption; not FDA-approved in the US (brand Hirudoid).

summary: Mucopolysaccharide polysulfate (MPS, a heparinoid; brand Hirudoid) is a topical preparation used for superficial thrombophlebitis and for the soothing relief of superficial bruising and hematoma, and more broadly (by region) for varicose-vein discomfort, blunt trauma, and sports injuries. It has heparin-like anticoagulant and fibrinolytic activity plus anti-inflammatory and anti-exudative effects, promoting resorption of hematoma and edema. It is applied topically (the UK SmPC directs 5-15 cm of cream/gel up to four times daily; many non-UK labels use a more conservative 3-5 cm one to three times daily). Standard strength is 0.3% (3 mg/g; 25,000 units/100 g), with a forte strength of 0.445%. Systemic absorption is low (about 0.3-4% over hours to days), so it has minimal systemic interactions and is acceptable in pregnancy and lactation. It must not be applied to broken/open skin, mucous membranes, large areas, or in children under 5 years. NOTE: Not FDA-approved in the US; this record is based on the UK/EMA SmPC, manufacturer, and Martindale references.

moa: The heparinoid mucopolysaccharide polysulfate exerts several overlapping local actions: an anticoagulant (heparin-like) effect that inhibits local thrombus formation; a thrombolytic/fibrinolytic effect that promotes dissolution of superficial clots and resorption of hematoma; an anti-inflammatory effect (weak inhibition of prostaglandin E2 synthesis, with indirect effects on leukotriene B4); and an anti-exudative (anti-edema) effect that reduces swelling and promotes resorption of edema. It also increases local skin blood flow (reported via nitric oxide). Systemic absorption from the skin is low, so these actions are essentially local.

lact: There is no evidence to suggest that the product should not be used during lactation, consistent with minimal systemic absorption.

pearls: Topical heparinoid (Hirudoid) for superficial venous and soft-tissue conditions - NOT a systemic anticoagulant
Used for superficial thrombophlebitis/phlebitis, bruises/hematoma, and varicose-vein discomfort
Standard strength 0.3% (3 mg/g; 25,000 U/100 g); forte 0.445% (4.45 mg/g)
Minimal systemic absorption - interactions and systemic adverse effects are essentially none
Do not apply to broken skin, mucous membranes, or large areas; not for children under 5
NOT FDA-approved in the US; dosing differs by country (UK SmPC 5-15 cm up to 4x/day vs non-UK 3-5 cm 1-3x/day) - follow the local label
missed: If you forget an application, apply it when you remember. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application; resume your usual schedule.
overdose: Topical overdose is very low risk given minimal absorption. There is no specific advice for accidental ingestion; provide general supportive measures if a large amount is swallowed.
